title: Unless a grain of wheat falls (John 12:12–26)
hookLine: a seed must fall into the earth and die to bear much fruit

lines: THE WORLD IS GONE AFTER HIM.
cards: The next day, the city is packed for Passover, and word spreads that Jesus is coming. A great crowd goes out to meet him.

John tells us what they carried: "Took branches of palm trees, and went forth to meet him, and cried, Hosanna: Blessed is the King of Israel that cometh in the name of the Lord." Hosanna is a Hebrew cry: save us, now.
Jesus finds a young donkey and rides in on it. The leaders watch and say: "behold, the world is gone after him." And then, as if to prove them right, some Greeks arrive.

teach.b: These Greeks are pilgrims, outsiders come to worship at the feast. They go to Philip and ask politely: "Sir, we would see Jesus." Philip tells Andrew, and together they tell Jesus.
Instead of bring them in, he says the hour has come, and talks about a seed.
"Verily, verily, I say unto you, Except a corn of wheat fall into the ground and die, it abideth alone: but if it die, it bringeth forth much fruit."
Corn, in the King James Bible, means any grain: here, a single grain of wheat.

teach.h: A GRAIN IN A JAR STAYS ALONE.
teach.b: Kept in a jar, it stays a grain forever: safe, whole, and alone.

Planted in the dark, it breaks open, stops being a seed, and becomes a stalk heavy with grain. Jesus is talking about his own death. The Greeks want to see him, and his answer is: the world will see me through my dying.
One grain becomes a harvest. Then, for anyone who follows him: "He that loveth his life shall lose it."
Not a call to despise life, but to let go of clutching it.

teach.h: EXCEPT A CORN OF WHEAT FALL.
teach.b: Dostoevsky put it at the front of The Brothers Karamazov, as the epigraph for the whole book. Farmers know it without any book: you can't eat your seed grain and have a harvest too.
Christians often read these words at funerals, and whenever something has to end so something else can begin.

how: Christians remember the entry into Jerusalem on Palm Sunday, often carrying palms; the grain of wheat saying is often read at funerals and in Holy Week.

games.q: some Greek pilgrims have come asking to see you. Philip and Andrew bring the message. what does Jesus say?
o: "the hour has come; a grain of wheat must fall and die."
"tell them to come back after the feast."
games.why: he speaks of a grain of wheat that must die to bear fruit. the world will see him through his death.

practice: Think of something you've been holding too tightly, an old plan that isn't working, a grudge, a version of yourself you've outgrown, a role, a possession, a need to be right, and hold it like a seed in your palm, noticing how hard you grip.
Then imagine opening your hand and letting it fall into the ground; you don't have to know what will grow. If you pray, place it in God's hands; if not, notice what your open hand feels like.
